blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for autonomous driving rely heavily on successful expert demonstrations, leaving model-specific failures underexploited.
Learning from these failures is hindered by unreliable diagnoses, poorly matched correction targets, and coarse rewards.
We propose RefineDrive , a failure-guided post-training framework that learns from self-generated failures through targeted supervision and safety-aware reinforcement learning.
Reliable Diagnosis derives structured, verifiable feedback on collisions and drivable-area violations directly from simulator states.
Minimum-Correction Target Retrieval searches a clustered human trajectory bank for nearby corrections that satisfy hard-safety constraints in the current scene, prioritizing preservation of the failed prediction’s motion pattern.
Conditioned on the driving context and failed trajectory, Correction SFT learns to generate the diagnosis followed by the retrieved correction as a training-only auxiliary task.
We then apply GRPO with a Safety-Layered Reward that strictly prioritizes hard-safe trajectories, retains continuous safety feedback for both unsafe and hard-safe trajectories, and rewards driving progress only after hard safety is satisfied.
At inference, the policy directly predicts trajectories from the driving context without an explicit diagnosis or repair stage.
On NAVSIM v1, RefineDrive improves the 4B base SFT policy from 87.7 to 91.7 PDMS.
Using the same checkpoint without additional training, RefineDrive achieves 89.4 EPDMS on the original NAVTEST scenes evaluated with NAVSIM v2 extended metrics.
Controlled ablations support the benefits of structured diagnosis supervision, retrieved corrections, and safety-layered optimization for direct planning.

blocks.en: Figure 1: Motivation and overview of RefineDrive. Existing failure-learning methods can suffer from unreliable VLM-based diagnoses, over-corrective human ground-truth supervision, and coarse aggregated rewards. We address these limitations with Reliable Diagnosis, which grounds structured feedback in NAVSIM PDM simulation; Minimum-Correction Target Retrieval, which searches a clustered human trajectory bank for safe corrections close to failed predictions; and Safety-Layered Reward, which provides hierarchical signals over hard safety, continuous safety, and driving progress.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown strong potential for end-to-end autonomous driving, benefiting from large-scale vision-language pretraining and expert demonstrations. However, most approaches still rely primarily on imitation learning from successful human behavior, while failures exposed by the model’s own rollouts—such as collisions and departures from the drivable area—remain underexploited. For a policy with strong basic driving capabilities, further improvement may depend less on imitating more expert behavior and more on identifying and correcting the remaining weaknesses revealed by its own failures.
blocks.zh: 远景-语言-行动(VLA)模式显示,通过大规模远景语言预训和专家示范,极有可能实现端到端自主驾驶。 然而,大多数方法仍然主要依靠从成功的人类行为中学习模仿,而模型本身推出的失败——例如碰撞和离开可驾驶区——仍然没有得到充分利用。 对于一个具有强大基本驱动能力的政策来说,进一步改进可能较少取决于模仿更多的专家行为,更多取决于识别和纠正其自身失败所揭示的其余弱点。

blocks.en:
Recent studies have begun to explore learning from failures, but three key limitations remain, as illustrated in Fig. 1 .
First, failure diagnosis can be unreliable . Methods that rely on large VLMs or teacher models to explain failures may produce open-ended diagnoses that are difficult to verify, with inaccurate event localization, incorrect causal attribution, or inconsistency with the simulated outcome.
Second, the correction target may be poorly matched to the failure . Since a failed trajectory is often only partially incorrect, directly replacing it with human ground truth can introduce unnecessary behavioral changes and lead to over-correction.
Third, coarse reward signals provide limited optimization guidance . An aggregated driving score may insufficiently distinguish the extent and timing of safety violations among unsafe trajectories or safety margins among safe ones, limiting fine-grained safety optimization.
blocks.zh:
最近的研究已开始探索从失败中吸取教训,但如图1所示,仍有三个关键局限。
首先,失败诊断可能不可靠。 依靠大型VLM或师范模型解释故障的方法可能会产生难以核实的开放式诊断,而事件本地化不准确,因果归属不正确,或与模拟结果不一致.
第二,修正目标可能与失败不相称。 由于一个失败的轨迹往往只是部分不正确,直接用人地真理来代替,可以引入不必要的行为变化,导致过度修正.
第三,粗细的奖励信号提供了有限的优化指导。 总的驾驶分数可能不足以区分不安全轨道中的安全违规程度和时间,或安全轨道中的安全幅度,限制了精细的安全优化。

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Vision-Language-Action Models for Autonomous Driving
blocks.zh: 2.1 自主驾驶的远景-语言-行动模式

blocks.en: Vision-language models (VLMs) have been applied to autonomous driving for scene understanding, reasoning, and decision making [ 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 , 5 ] . DriveVLM [ 6 ] emphasizes language-space reasoning for hierarchical planning, whereas VLA models more tightly integrate multimodal reasoning and action generation. OpenDriveVLA [ 7 ] aligns instance-aware visual and language representations for autoregressive actions, while AutoVLA [ 8 ] combines semantic reasoning, discretized action tokens, and reinforcement fine-tuning. ReCogDrive [ 9 ] integrates a cognitive VLM with a diffusion planner, and Qwen-Drive [ 10 ] explores unified representations for perception, understanding, and planning.
blocks.zh: 愿景语言模型(VLMs)已被应用于自主驱动以了解场景,推理,和决策[1,2,3,4,5]. 驱动VLM [6]强调分级规划的语言-空间推理,而VLA模型则更紧密地融合了多式联运推理和动作生成. 打开驱动程序VLA [7] 将实例感知的视觉和语言表现配合自动递减动作,而AutoVLA [8] 结合语义推理,碟形动作符,加固微调. ReCogDrive [9] 将认知VLM与传播计划器融合,Quen-Drive [10] 探索统一的表达方式,用于感知,理解和规划.

blocks.en: ReflectDrive [ 11 ] introduces discrete-diffusion planning with inference-time safety reflection: a safety scorer identifies unsafe waypoints, local search finds safe anchors, and inpainting regenerates the surrounding trajectory. Although both methods repair unsafe predictions, ReflectDrive performs waypoint-level inference editing, whereas we retrieve complete, scene-validated trajectories and pair them with structured diagnoses as offline Correction SFT supervision.
blocks.zh: ReflectDrive [11] 引入了带推论时间安全反射的离散分散规划:安全计分器识别不安全的路标,局部搜索找到安全锚,并涂抹再生周边轨迹. 虽然两种方法都修复了不安全的预测, ReflectDrive进行路标级推论编辑,而我们则检索完整的,场景验证的轨迹,并配以结构化的诊断作为离线校正SFT监督.

blocks.en: 2.2 Learning from Failures
blocks.zh: 2.2 从失败中学习

blocks.en: Learning from failures complements imitation from successful demonstrations. ChauffeurNet [ 12 ] perturbs expert trajectories to synthesize unsafe situations. Recent VLA methods exploit failures more directly: ELF-VLA [ 13 ] uses teacher-generated diagnoses for trajectory refinement, SafeAlign-VLA [ 14 ] constructs failure descriptions and counterfactual positives for supervised and reinforcement learning, and FIRE-VLA [ 15 ] employs failure-triggered self-distillation with privileged future information. Rather than relying on open-ended teacher explanations, we derive structured diagnoses directly from simulator states, grounding violation times, involved objects, and boundary-exit directions in verifiable geometric and kinematic evidence.
blocks.zh: 从失败中学习是对成功示威的模仿。 ChauffeurNet [12] 扰动专家轨迹合成不安全情况. 最近VLA方法更直接地利用故障:ELF-VLA [13] 使用教师生成的诊断方法来改进轨迹,SafeAlign-VLA [14] 构建故障描述和反事实阳性,用于有监督的强化学习,FIRE-VLA [15] 使用故障触发自沉,并有特殊的未来信息. 我们不是依靠开放式的教师解释,而是直接从模拟状态、违反时间、涉及物体和边界出境方向等可核查的几何和动态证据中得出结构化诊断。

blocks.en:
The concurrent R 2 LPL framework [ 16 ] retrieves feasible trajectory anchors from recoverable closed-loop states and
updates an anchor-scoring planner through replay-based lifelong learning. Its target scores combine rule-based planning quality with route and expert consistency using state-dependent weights. Both methods construct corrective supervision from policy failures, but differ in the correction setting and target-selection criterion. We formulate our correction stage as trajectory-conditioned behavior repair as a training-only auxiliary task: the failed prediction serves as both the reference for retrieving a nearby, scene-verified safe trajectory from a clustered human trajectory bank and an explicit conditioning input for Correction SFT. Rather than supervising anchor scores, we train the VLA to autoregressively generate a simulator-grounded diagnosis followed by the corrected trajectory. Safety-Layered GRPO subsequently refines the policy.

通过基于重播的终身学习更新主播评分计划员. 其目标分数将基于规则的规划质量与路线和专家一致性相结合,使用国家依赖权重. 这两种方法都从政策失误中构建了纠正性监督,但在纠正的设定和目标选择标准上有所不同。 我们将校正阶段发展为轨迹条件行为修复,仅作为训练辅助任务:失败的预测既作为从群聚的人类轨迹库中检索附近经现场核实的安全轨迹的参考,又作为校正SFT的明确条件输入. 我们不监督锚分数,而是训练VLA 自动地产生一个模拟器的基础诊断,然后修正轨迹。 安全-Layered GRPO随后完善了这项政策。

blocks.en: 3 Method
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en: 3.1 Overview
blocks.zh: 3.1 概览

blocks.en:
We propose RefineDrive that enables an already capable driving VLA to improve from safety-critical failures exposed by its own behavior.
As illustrated in Fig. 2 , our framework consists of four stages: (1) Failure Discovery , (2) Structured Failure Correction , (3) Correction SFT ,
and (4) Safety-Layered Reinforcement Learning .
blocks.zh:
我们提出完善的驱动力,使已经有能力的驱动VLA能够从自身行为暴露的安全关键故障中改进.
如图2所示,我们的框架包括四个阶段: (1) 故障发现,(2) 结构化故障纠正,(3) 更正SFT,
(4) 安全辅导强化学习。

blocks.en: The resulting framework progressively improves the policy by focusing learning on weaknesses revealed by its own rollouts rather than repeatedly imitating already-mastered expert behavior.
blocks.zh: 由此形成的框架逐步改进了政策,将学习重点放在自身推出的弱点上,而不是反复模仿已经掌握的专家行为。

blocks.en: 3.2 Failure Discovery
blocks.zh: 3.2 失败发现

blocks.en:
We start from a supervised fine-tuned driving policy and perform offline rollouts on the training scenarios.
Each predicted trajectory is re-executed using the NAVSIM PDM Simulator to obtain reproducible safety outcomes.
blocks.zh:
我们从一个经过监督的微调的驾驶政策开始,对培训方案进行线下推广。
每个预测的轨迹都使用NAVSIM PDM模拟器重新执行,以获得可复制的安全结果.

They therefore provide targeted cases for subsequent diagnosis and correction.

blocks.en: 3.3 Structured Failure Correction
blocks.zh: 3.3 结构性故障纠正

blocks.en: For each discovered failure, we construct correction supervision that answers two complementary questions: why does the current prediction fail? and what is the smallest behavioral change that makes it safe? We address them through verifiable failure diagnosis and counterfactual minimal correction.
blocks.zh: 对于每一个发现的失败,我们构建校正监督,以回答两个互补的问题:为什么目前的预测失败? 什么是最小的行为改变 使它安全? 我们通过可核查的失败诊断和反事实的最低限度纠正来解决它们。

blocks.en: Rather than relying on a teacher VLM to produce open-ended explanations, we derive failure feedback directly from simulator states.
blocks.zh: 我们不是依靠教师的VLM来产生开放式的解释,而是直接从模拟状态得到故障反馈.

blocks.en:
For an at-fault collision, we identify the first ego at-fault collision and extract its occurrence time, object category, and relative position with respect to the ego vehicle.
The corresponding traffic participant is further projected onto the current front-view image to obtain its 2D bounding box.
The resulting feedback explicitly indicates when the collision occurs, which object is involved, and where the object appears in the current visual observation.
blocks.zh:
对于一次偶发碰撞,我们确定第一次偶发碰撞的自我并提取其发生时间,物体类别,以及相对于自发飞行器的相对位置.
相应的交通参与者被进一步投射到目前的前视图像上,以获得其2D边框.
由此产生的反馈明确显示碰撞发生时间,涉及哪个物体,以及物体在当前视觉观测中出现的位置.

blocks.en: For a drivable-area violation, we identify the first time at which the predicted trajectory leaves the valid driving region and determine whether the ego vehicle exits through the left or right boundary.
blocks.zh: 对于可驾驶区域侵犯,我们确定预测的轨迹首次离开有效驾驶区域,并确定自负车辆是否通过左侧或右侧边界退出。

blocks.en: When the collision object cannot be reliably localized in the current visual observation, we discard the corresponding sample to avoid introducing textual supervision that cannot be grounded in the model input.
blocks.zh: 当碰撞物体无法在目前的视觉观察中可靠地定位时,我们丢弃相应的样本,以避免引入无法基于模型输入的文字监督.

blocks.en: The resulting diagnosis is therefore derived from reproducible geometric and kinematic verification rather than subjective model interpretation.
blocks.zh: 因此,由此产生的诊断来源于可复制的几何学和运动学验证,而不是主观的模型解释.

blocks.en:
For an already capable driving policy, a failed trajectory’s maneuver intention and most of its future motion may remain reasonable, with only a limited deviation causing the safety violation.
Direct replacement with the human trajectory may introduce unnecessary behavioral changes; we instead search for a nearby feasible correction from a real human trajectory bank.
blocks.zh:
对于已经有能力的驾驶政策来说,轨迹失败的操纵意图及其大部分未来运动可能依然合理,只有有限的偏差导致安全受损。
直接替换人类的轨迹可能会带来不必要的行为改变;我们反而从真正的人类轨迹库中寻找附近的可行的修正。

blocks.en:
We construct the bank from the training set and group trajectories by motion pattern using K-Means.
Given a failed trajectory τ − \tau^{-} , we identify its assigned cluster in the same feature space and search it first to preserve the original motion pattern.
If no feasible correction is found, we search the remaining clusters in ascending order of the distance from their centers to the feature representation of τ − \tau^{-} .

blocks.en: 3.5 Safety-Layered Reward
blocks.zh: 3.5 安全奖励

blocks.en:
We refine the corrected policy with GRPO using a reward that combines hard safety , continuous safety assessment , and driving progress .
Hard-safety feasibility is determined by F ⁡ ( τ ) ∈ { 0 , 1 } F(\tau)\in\{0,1\} in Eq. 2 , which requires NC, DAC, and TTC to be satisfied simultaneously.

Binary feasibility alone cannot distinguish failure severity among
unsafe trajectories or safety margins among feasible ones.
We therefore construct a continuous safety score from simulator-derived
margins and violation times.
For each safety factor k ∈ { clr , ttc , road } k\in\{\mathrm{clr},\mathrm{ttc},\mathrm{road}\} ,
corresponding to obstacle clearance, TTC safety, and drivable-area
compliance, let m k ​ ( τ ) m_{k}(\tau) denote its minimum signed margin and t k ​ ( τ ) t_{k}(\tau) its first violation time.
We normalize them as m ¯ k ​ ( τ ) = clip ⁡ ( m k ​ ( τ ) − l k u k − l k , 0 , 1 ) , t ¯ k ​ ( τ ) = clip ⁡ ( t k ​ ( τ ) T , 0 , 1 ) , \bar{m}_{k}(\tau)=\operatorname{clip}\left(\frac{m_{k}(\tau)-l_{k}}{u_{k}-l_{k}},0,1\right),\qquad\bar{t}_{k}(\tau)=\operatorname{clip}\left(\frac{t_{k}(\tau)}{T},0,1\right), (7) where [ l k , u k ] [l_{k},u_{k}] is the factor-specific normalization interval
and T T is the simulation horizon.
We set t k ​ ( τ ) = T t_{k}(\tau)=T when the corresponding violation does not occur.
The continuous safety score is S ⁡ ( τ ) = ∑ k w k ​ [ ( 1 − ρ k ) ​ m ¯ k ​ ( τ ) + ρ k ​ t ¯ k ​ ( τ ) ] , ∑ k w k = 1 , S(\tau)=\sum_{k}w_{k}\left[(1-\rho_{k})\bar{m}_{k}(\tau)+\rho_{k}\bar{t}_{k}(\tau)\right],\qquad\sum_{k}w_{k}=1, (8) where w k ≥ 0 w_{k}\geq 0 and ρ k ∈ [ 0 , 1 ] \rho_{k}\in[0,1] , ensuring S ⁡ ( τ ) ∈ [ 0 , 1 ] S(\tau)\in[0,1] .
Higher scores favor larger safety margins and later violations.
Thus, S S provides graded feedback on failure severity for unsafe
trajectories while continuing to distinguish safety margins among
hard-safe trajectories.

We reward driving progress only after hard safety is satisfied.
The progress score is defined using Ego Progress (EP): P ⁡ ( τ ) = EP ⁡ ( τ ) P(\tau)=\mathrm{EP}(\tau) (9) The final reward is R ⁡ ( τ ) = λ F ​ F ​ ( τ ) + λ S ​ [ 1 − η ​ F ​ ( τ ) ] ​ S ​ ( τ ) + λ P ​ F ​ ( τ ) ​ P ​ ( τ ) , R(\tau)=\lambda_{F}F(\tau)+\lambda_{S}\bigl[1-\eta F(\tau)\bigr]S(\tau)+\lambda_{P}F(\tau)P(\tau), (10) where η ∈ [ 0 , 1 ] \eta\in[0,1] controls the attenuation of the continuous
safety reward once hard safety is satisfied.
Unsafe trajectories receive only λ S ​ S ​ ( τ ) \lambda_{S}S(\tau) .
Hard-safe trajectories receive the feasibility bonus, retain a
reduced safety-score weight of λ S ​ ( 1 − η ) \lambda_{S}(1-\eta) , and additionally
receive the progress reward.

We set ( λ F , λ S , λ P ) = ( 2.0 , 1.0 , 0.25 ) (\lambda_{F},\lambda_{S},\lambda_{P})=(2.0,1.0,0.25) and η = 0.5 \eta=0.5 , retaining half of the continuous safety weight for
hard-safe trajectories.
Consequently, unsafe trajectories have R ⁡ ( τ ) ∈ [ 0 , 1 ] R(\tau)\in[0,1] , whereas
hard-safe trajectories have R ⁡ ( τ ) ∈ [ 2 , 2.75 ] R(\tau)\in[2,2.75] .
This guarantees a strict reward preference for hard-safe trajectories
while preserving fine-grained safety feedback within both groups.
4 Experiments
blocks.zh: 4 实验

blocks.en: 4.1 Experimental Setup
blocks.zh: 4.1 实验设置

blocks.en:
We conduct experiments on NAVSIM [ 17 ] , a planning-oriented autonomous driving benchmark built on OpenScene/nuPlan.
Following the official NAVSIM v1 protocol, we use NAVTRAIN for supervised training, failure mining, and reinforcement learning, and reserve NAVTEST exclusively for evaluation.
All corrective trajectories are constructed from the training split only.
We additionally evaluate the same checkpoint used for NAVSIM v1
on the original NAVTEST scenes using the extended metrics of NAVSIM v2 [ 18 ] ,
without additional training.
This is a single-stage, original-scene evaluation and does not include
synthetic second-stage observations or two-stage pseudo-simulation
aggregation.
blocks.zh:
我们在NAVSIM [17]上进行实验,这是基于OpenScene/nuPlan的面向规划的自主驱动基准.
根据NAVSIM v1正式协议,我们使用NAVTRAIN进行监督培训、失败开采和强化学习,并将NAVTEST专用于评估。
所有矫正轨迹都只从训练中划分出来。
我们还评估了NAVSIM v1使用的同一检查站。
使用NAVSIM v2 [18] 的扩展度量,
未经额外培训。
这是单阶段的原创评价,不包括
合成第二阶段观测或两阶段伪模拟
汇总。

blocks.en:
We report Predictive Driver Model Score (PDMS) for overall
benchmark comparison. To evaluate our safety-oriented
objective, we analyze No At-Fault Collision (NC),
Drivable Area Compliance (DAC), and Time-to-Collision (TTC)
as the key safety outcomes, alongside Ego Progress (EP)
and Comfort (C). We interpret safety and progress jointly:
similar aggregate PDMS values need not imply similar
safety performance. All metrics are higher-is-better.
blocks.zh:
我们报告总体预测性驱动模型分数(PDMS)
基准比较。 评估我们的安全
目标,我们分析无过失碰撞(NC),
可流动区域合规(DAC)和时间与收集(TTC)
作为关键安全成果,与Ego进步(EP)
和舒适(C)。 我们共同解释安全和进展:
类似的聚合 PDMS 值不一定意味着类似
安全性能。 所有度量衡都比现在更好

blocks.en:
We instantiate RefineDrive with Qwen3.5-4B and first perform trajectory
SFT on NAVTRAIN.
The resulting policy is rolled out to mine safety-critical failures,
from which we construct the diagnosis-and-correction dataset.
We then perform Correction SFT followed by Safety-Layered GRPO.
All ablations start from the same base SFT checkpoint.
During evaluation, every checkpoint, including those evaluated
immediately after Correction SFT, directly predicts eight ( x , y , heading ) (x,y,\mathrm{heading}) waypoints at 0.5 0.5 s intervals over a 4 4 s horizon from the current front-view image, ego state, and
historical trajectory.
No failed trajectory is supplied, and no additional diagnosis or trajectory-repair pass is performed.
blocks.zh:
我们用 Qwen3.5-4B 进行精确飞行,并首先执行轨迹
(原始内容存档于2018-05-21). SFT on NavTRAIN.
由此产生的政策被推广到对地雷安全至关重要的失败,
我们从中构建诊断和校正数据集。
然后我们进行SFT的校正,然后是Safety-Layered GRPO。
所有事件都从同一基地的SFT检查站开始。
在评价期间,每个检查站,包括被评价的检查站
校正 SFT 后,从当前前视图像,自我状态,以及
历史轨迹。
没有提供故障轨迹,也没有进行额外的诊断或轨迹修复。

blocks.en: 4.3 Ablation Studies
blocks.zh: 4.3 阅读研究

blocks.en:
We conduct controlled ablations on NAVSIM v1 to study:
(1) learning from self-generated failures;
(2) minimal correction versus Human GT;
(3) the benefit of structured failure-diagnosis supervision; and
(4) Safety-Layered Reward versus direct PDMS optimization.
All variants share the same base SFT model and evaluation protocol, and
Human-GT and minimal-correction variants use the same failure cases.

Table 3: Ablation of failure-aware Correction SFT.
Human GT and Minimal use the same failure cases and identical
structured diagnosis supervision.
Minimal w/o Diagnosis retains the same corrective trajectory
targets as Minimal but removes diagnosis supervision.

目标为最小,但取消了诊断监督。

blocks.en:
Using self-generated failures with Human GT supervision improves NAVTEST PDMS from 87.7 to 88.2.
With the failure cases and structured diagnosis supervision held fixed,
replacing Human GT with retrieved minimal corrections further increases PDMS to 88.6, with gains in NC, DAC, EP, and TTC.
Across the 32,650 paired Correction-SFT records, however, the retrieved
targets have a slightly lower mean PDMS than the corresponding Human GT trajectories (95.4 vs. 95.8).
Thus, the downstream improvement cannot be explained by higher average target PDMS. Furthermore, removing diagnosis supervision while keeping the corrective
trajectory targets unchanged reduces PDMS from 88.6 to 88.3.
This suggests that structured failure-diagnosis supervision benefits
the resulting planning policy beyond corrective trajectory supervision alone.

Together, these comparisons support a safety-oriented
contribution from diagnosis-and-correction supervision
after RL, with an explicit progress trade-off.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: We present RefineDrive, a failure-guided post-training framework integrating Reliable Diagnosis, Minimum-Correction Target Retrieval, and Safety-Layered GRPO, with no inference-time diagnosis or repair. Controlled ablations show that diagnosis-and-correction supervision improves NC, DAC, and TTC after RL at some cost to progress, while Safety-Layered Reward improves all three at the same mean EP as direct PDMS optimization. RefineDrive achieves 91.7 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 and, with the same checkpoint and no further training, 89.4 EPDMS on the original NAVTEST scenes under NAVSIM v2 extended metrics.
blocks.zh: 我们提出 " 精益求精 " ,这是一个由故障指导的培训后框架,其中包含可靠的诊断、最低校正目标检索和安全-Layered GRPO,没有推断时间诊断或修复。 受控浮雕显示,诊断和校正监督在RL之后以某种成本改进了NC、DAC和TTC,而Safety-Layeed Reward则在与直接PDMS优化相同的平均EP上改进了所有三种。 完善Drive在NAVSIM v1上实现91.7 PDMS,在相同的检查站和没有进一步培训的情况下,在NAVSIM v2扩展度量衡下对NAVTEST的原始场景实现89.4 EPDMS.
